newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends week mixed, demand weak.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends week mixed, demand weak.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed on Friday but sentiment remained weak due to an absence of consumer demand, traders said.
Activity was also thin as most players in the region were making their way to Hatyai, Thailand, to attend an industry function, said the traders.
The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted June RSS 1 at 276 cents ($) a kg, up half cent from Wednesday. May SMR 20 buyer fell one cent to 259.90.
"There were no sales, no leads. I don't see anything changing next week," said a trader.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 258 cents a kg, SMR CV at 331, SMR L at 309, SMR 5 at 256, SMR 10 at 269 and latex at 227.
They expected prices to fall by around three to five cents next week. This week, the RSS1 was down by 1.50 cents and SMR20 4.0 cents.
Traders said the Thai government's intervention in its domestic market and a strike at US-based Goodyear did not bother players.
